questions.q: What is the stated purpose of Milton's Paradise Lost?
options: To chronicle the English Civil War
To justify the ways of God to men
To praise the reign of Oliver Cromwell
To explain the origins of the universe
questions.explanation: Milton states this explicitly in the opening lines of Book 1.

questions.q: How many books did the second edition (1674) of Paradise Lost contain?
questions.explanation: The original 1667 edition had 10 books, but it was reorganized into 12 for the second edition.

questions.q: Who speaks the line 'Better to reign in Hell, than serve in Heaven' in Paradise Lost?
questions.explanation: Satan says this in Book 1, establishing his rebellious character.

questions.q: Milton's 'Areopagitica' is a passionate defense of:
questions.explanation: It is a famous prose polemic against licensing and censorship.

questions.q: Which major physical disability afflicted Milton during the writing of his greatest works?
questions.explanation: Milton went completely blind in 1652 and had to dictate his late masterpieces.

questions.q: Which of Milton's works is a 'closet drama' about a blind biblical hero?
questions.explanation: Samson Agonistes tells the story of the blinded Samson and parallels Milton's own life.

questions.q: In what poetic form is Paradise Lost written?
questions.explanation: It is written in unrhymed iambic pentameter, or blank verse.

questions.q: Milton's 'Lycidas' is a pastoral elegy written to mourn the death of:
questions.explanation: He wrote it to commemorate his Cambridge friend, Edward King.
